And if the Shechinah is not there - "and the sun goes down" - the Holy One, blessed be He, withdraws from it, and it remains in darkness, and several destroyers and several evil sufferings that are not sufferings of love rule over it - this is what is written (Deuteronomy 31:17), "is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us?" - for these evils find him at every time and moment, of which it is said (Job 7:18), "and You visit him every morning, and try him every moment." And what causes the Shechinah not to rest upon him, and the sun not to shine upon him? Because of the breath of falsehood and words of falsehood that go forth from his mouth - and therefore (Ecclesiastes 8:14), "there is a vanity [hevel] which is done upon the earth" - there is one "hevel" and another "hevel." There is a "hevel" from the masters of falsehood, of whom it is said (Jeremiah 10:15), "they are vanity [hevel], the work of delusion" - for they err [to'im] in the vanity of falsehood. And there is a "hevel" of which it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3), "for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of YHVH does man live" - and this is the "hevel" of Torah, which is the heh, the five books of the Torah from the bet of "Bereshit" to the lamed of "le'einei kol Yisrael" ["before the eyes of all Israel," the last word of the Torah] - and this is "hevel" [comprising heh and vet-lamed, forming the letters heh-bet-lamed = hevel] - to this point.

Behold, that the evil "hevel" removes the Shechinah and the Holy One, blessed be He, from a person, and then suffering rules over him - but the "hevel" of Torah is not so, but rather brings life to a person, as he says, "by everything that proceeds from the mouth of YHVH does man live." And whoever wishes to be cleaved to his God shall diminish even things necessary for him and increase silence, as explained on the verse (Psalms 34:13), "who is the man who desires life" - for the essence of life is cleaving, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are all alive" - "and keep your tongue from evil," as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:50: Further, in the Book of Ezekiel (18:5-9): "but if a man be just, and do that which is lawful and right, and has not eaten upon the mountains, neither has lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, neither has defiled his neighbor's wife, neither has come near to a menstruous woman, and has not wronged any, but has restored the debtor his pledge, has robbed none by violence, has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment, he who has not given forth upon usury, neither has taken any increase, who has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, has executed true judgment between man and man, has walked in My statutes, and has kept My judgments, to deal truly - he is just, he shall surely live."

Further, he should be careful concerning the aspects of good fear explained in the Gate of Fear, of which Solomon said (Proverbs 10:27), "the fear of the LORD prolongs days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened," and likewise (ibid. 14:27), "the fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death." And to keep the disciplines of the Torah, as it is written (ibid. 4:13), "take fast hold of discipline; let her not go; keep her, for she is your life," and it says (ibid. 10:17), "he is in the way of life who heeds discipline, but he who forsakes reproof leads astray."

Further, it is fitting that he rise early for the synagogue to be counted among the first ten, which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 8a) lengthens one's days, and they proved this from the verse (ibid. 8:35), "for whoever finds Me finds life." And this aspect is efficacious, especially if he is the first, provided he prays in that same synagogue where he was among the first ten - and so I received from my teacher, peace be upon him, that the reward our Rabbis, of blessed memory, mentioned for coming among the first ten applies only to one who prays there, and this is also proven from the words of the Zohar in Parashat Naso.

Also, a great help for the penitent, that he be aided by the Creator during the day, is if he rises early to read Torah and pray over his iniquities, as it is written (Psalms 88:2), "O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before You" - and we elaborated on this in the Gate of Holiness.

Further, he should also be careful with the commandment of tefillin, which is explained as lengthening the days of one who dons them, as it is written (Isaiah 38:16), "O LORD, by these things men live" - so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Menachot (44b). And it is fitting that a penitent have two pairs of tefillin, one according to the view of Rashi, peace be upon him, and one according to the view of Rabbenu Tam, peace be upon him - and at the time of the Shacharit prayer he should wear both pairs in order to fulfill the commandment of the Shema properly, so that he not be said to be testifying false testimony against himself, since the tefillin of one are invalid according to the other, and thus he would have recited the Shema without [valid] tefillin according to one view; and the rest of the day he should wear the tefillin according to Rabbenu Tam's view. And whenever his body is found clean, he should wear them, and find himself aided by the Creator - for they said there, in chapter HaTecheilet, Rav Sheshet said, whoever does not don tefillin transgresses eight positive commandments, and so on - and from the negative you infer the affirmative, that one who dons them fulfills eight positive commandments.

Further, he should pursue charity in secret, as it is written (Proverbs 21:14), "a gift in secret pacifies anger." And the charity that bears fruit above is the charity done for its own sake without any ulterior motive - and if he intends it along the secret path, how good is his portion! And in charity "life" is mentioned, as it is said (ibid. 12:28), "in the way of righteousness is life, and in that pathway there is no death," and likewise (ibid. 16:31), "the hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness."

And especially on the day of the fast, it is fitting to give as charity the portion of food he would have eaten at the morning meal, so as not to gain, from his fast, only a lack of distribution [to others] - and it appears to me that one can be precise about a matter in the words of the prophet, who said (Isaiah 58:7), "is it not to share your bread with the hungry" - "your bread," which was due to be your own portion - to exclude giving the portion of his wife and children, whom he is obligated to sustain, if he does not have enough to support them except sparingly - at least he shall give his own portion.

And so he should pursue acts of kindness, as it is written (Proverbs 21:21), "he who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor." And they said in Rosh Hashanah (18a), in these words: Abaye and Rava came from the house of Eli - Rava, who occupied himself with Torah [alone], lived forty years; Abaye, who occupied himself with Torah and acts of kindness, lived sixty years - to this point.

And concerning the matter of occupation with Torah and acts of kindness, which takes precedence, they explained in the Yerushalmi (Chagigah, chapter 1, halachah 7): Rabbi Yehuda, when he would see the funeral procession and the bridal procession competing [for the road], would fix his eyes on his students and say, deed takes precedence over study - they voted in the upper chamber of Beit Arim that study takes precedence over deed. Rabbi Abahu was in Caesarea; he sent his son Rabbi Chanina to acquire merit [collecting for burial] in Tiberias. They sent and said to him, he is a doer of kindness [gomel chesed]. He sent a letter to him: is it for lack of graves in Caesarea that I sent you to Tiberias? They have already voted in the upper chamber of Beit Arim in Lod that study takes precedence over deed. The Rabbis of Caesarea said, this applies where there is someone else to do the deed, but where there is no one else to do the deed, the deed takes precedence over study - to this point.

Further, they said, of blessed memory, in the Pesikta, on the verse (Psalms 16:11), "You shall make known to me the path of life": Rabbi Yudan said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, make known to me the path of life. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, David, you desire life? Look to fear, as it is said (Proverbs 10:27), "the fear of the LORD prolongs days." Rabbi Ze'ira said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, Master of the universe, make known to me the path of life. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, David, you desire life? Look to suffering, as it is written (ibid. 6:23), "and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life." Rav said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, make known to me the path of life. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, David, you desire life? Look to Torah, as it is written (ibid. 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it." Another interpretation: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, cast off your doubt - do and eat, as it is said, "keep My commandments, and live" - to this point. And these four aspects correspond to the four letters of the Name in their order, for one versed in the appellations of the Zohar. And therefore each of them has "life" in it, in the way that each letter of the Name comprises the whole Name, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, page 92a), and my teacher, peace be upon him, explained there in Sefer HaSha'ar, the Name of forty-two letters.

Further, he should be careful, for one who toils in his study in private does not quickly forget - and so they expounded (Sukkah 49b), "the curves of your thighs are like ornaments" (Song of Songs 7:2) - just as the thigh is in secret, so words of Torah [should be studied] in secret - and since one who occupies himself with Torah in secret becomes wise, behold it is written (Ecclesiastes 7:12), "wisdom gives life to those who have it."

And in his reading of Torah, he should utter the words with his mouth, which brings about remembrance and length of days, as we say in Eruvin (54a), in these words: Shmuel said to Rabbi Yehuda, sharp one, open your mouth and read, open your mouth and study, so that it be fixed in you and prolong your life, as it is said (Proverbs 4:22), "for they are life to those who find them, and health to all his flesh" - do not read "le-motze'eihem" [to those who find them] but "le-motzi'eihem" [to those who utter them] with the mouth - to this point, and this too is efficacious.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:62: And if he thirsts on the day of the fast because of the reading, he should consider this as atonement for the sin of idle words, as they said in Tractate Yoma (77a): Rav Nachman said, from here (Jeremiah 2:25), "withhold your foot from being unshod, and your throat from thirst" - withhold yourself from sin, so that your foot not come to being unshod; withhold your tongue from idle words, so that your throat not come to thirst - to this point. And Rashi explained "so that your foot not come to being unshod" as referring to going into exile - to this point. And along these lines is the thirst - it follows that the thirst of exile atones for idle words, and the same applies to the thirst of the fast a person accepts upon himself to atone for his iniquity, especially through occupation with Torah, of which it is written (Proverbs 15:4), "a wholesome tongue is a tree of life."

Further, he should be careful not to become angry, and should grasp the attribute of humility, which is explained in the Gate of Humility as also having "life" mentioned in it, as it is written (ibid. 22:4), "by humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, honor, and life." And further it is written (Isaiah 57:15), "I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite." And we have already elaborated in the Gate of Humility that there is nothing that removes the Shechinah, and likewise the soul, from a person except anger - and then it is said of him (Deuteronomy 31:17), "is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us" - and in this matter the penitent must be more careful than in anything else.

And it is said in Sefer Chassidim (section 649): an incident with a certain pious man, of whom they asked, to what do you attribute your length of days? He said, because no person ever cursed me or insulted me that I answered him, but I would endure it and forgive whoever caused me distress - to this point.

Further, in Avot D'Rabbi Natan (34:10), they said, ten things are called "life": the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:10), "He is the living God." Torah is called "life," as it is written (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life." Israel is called "life," as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are all alive this day." The wise are called "life," as it is said (Proverbs 13:14), "the teaching of the wise is a fountain of life." The righteous are called "life," as it is said (ibid. 11:30), "the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life." The Garden of Eden, as it is written (Genesis 2:9), "and the tree of life in the midst of the garden." Water, as it is said (Genesis 26:19), "living water." The Land of Israel, as it is said (Ezekiel 26:20), "and I shall set glory in the land of the living." Jerusalem, as it is said (Psalms 116:9), "I shall walk before the LORD in the lands of the living." Acts of kindness, as it is said (ibid. 63:4), "for Your kindness is better than life; my lips shall praise You" - to this point.

And all these ten things have practical implications - and even though it is not our way, in this composition, to explain the discourses of our Rabbis, as we stated in the Introduction, nevertheless we saw fit to explain the general intent of this discourse, because of the benefits that follow from it.

And we say that he intended to explain the levels a person needs in order to cleave to his Owner, so as to attain the secret of the supernal life - for He, may He be exalted, is the source of life for all existing things, as he says (Nehemiah 9:6), "and You give life to them all" - and by cleaving to Him, a person cleaves to life, as the liturgical poet said, "if I cleave to You, my life is even in my death." And therefore he said that the essential, first cleaving is to Him who brought everything into being, who is the cause of life for all worlds, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:10), "He is the living God, and the everlasting King" - and to cleave to His Torah, for the Torah is the revelation of His divinity to us, as we shall explain in the coming chapter, for He and His Torah are all one.

Further, that he cleave to Israel, because their holy souls flow from the source of supernal life, as he says (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God" - and this is (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God are all alive" - the meaning being, because you are cleaved to His Name, which is the source of life, as it is written, "He is the living God," therefore you are called "living."

Therefore it is not fitting for a person of Israel to mingle in partnership with an idol-worshipping gentile, as explained concerning (Leviticus 25:14), "or buy of your neighbor's hand" - and so they explained in Tractate Megillah (28a), concerning what we say there, that it is forbidden to gaze at the image of a wicked person - they said, of blessed memory: Avuha bar Ihi and Binyamin bar Ihi - one said, credit is due to me for never having gazed at a gentile; and the other said, credit is due to me for never having formed a partnership with a gentile - to this point. And it has already been explained in the Gate of Repentance, chapter 8, that the reason for [the prohibition of] gazing at the image of a wicked person is that it implants in one's heart that spirit of impurity that shows itself in his face, and from this follows confusion of thought and the nullification of cleaving. And therefore the author of the discourse comes to teach us that Israel is called "life," so that they not engage in business dealings except with Israel, who are called "life," and this not bring upon him the disruption of cleaving.

Further, that he cleave to the wise and the righteous, who are called "life" - and the intent is that He, blessed be He, dwells within them, and by cleaving to them, one cleaves to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:20), "and to Him shall you cleave" - and is it possible for a person to cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He? Rather, that he cleave to Torah scholars - and so too "you shall fear the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 10:20) includes Torah scholars (Pesachim 22b).

And the Garden of Eden is called "life," to teach that the essence of cleaving to Torah, the wise, and the righteous is in order to merit the World to Come - for the essential dwelling of the soul is in the World to Come, where the Tree of Life is in the midst of the garden, as was Adam, the first man, before his sin - and he should not do his deeds nor occupy himself with Torah for any worldly cause, for then his Torah does not ascend above. And so they expounded in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, end of page 223), on the verse (Ecclesiastes 1:3), "what profit has a man of all his labor which he takes under the sun?" - he says there, that the labor of Torah that is above the sun [i.e., pure Torah study] is different; Rabbi Chiya said, even the labor of Torah, when one labors in it for the sake of people, or for his own honor, is written "under the sun," for it does not ascend above - to this point.

Water, as it is said, "living water" - a further great cause of cleaving is that one purify himself in the waters of the mikveh, and we have already explained and elaborated on this in the Gate of Love (chapter 11), concerning "purity brings one to holiness" - and especially if the mikveh is from living water, which purifies a zav and a zavah - certainly it is a greater aid to cleaving.

The Land of Israel - it is known that prophecy rests only in the Land of Israel, and the Land of Israel has several virtues, one of them being that no external force has dominion or providence there, as it is written (Deuteronomy 11:12), "the eyes of the LORD your God are always upon it" - and they said in the Midrash (Shocher Tov), on the verse (Psalms 105:4), "seek the LORD and His strength; seek His face continually": Rabbi Yosi bar Chalafta said to Rabbi Yishmael his son, do you wish to see the Shechinah in this world? Occupy yourself with Torah in the Land of Israel, as it is said, "seek the LORD and His strength; seek His face continually" - to this point. And the explanation of "seek the LORD and His strength" - Torah is called "strength" [oz], as it is said (ibid. 29:11), "the LORD will give strength to His people." "Seek His face continually" - this is the Land of Israel, of which it is said (Deuteronomy 11:12), "always, the eyes of the LORD your God are upon it."

And further, concerning the virtue of dwelling in the Land of Israel, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 72b), in these words: Rabbi Yehuda said, happy is the portion of whoever merits to make his dwelling in the holy land - for whoever merits it merits to be drawn from the supernal dew of heaven that descends upon the land, and whoever merits to be bound, in his lifetime, to this holy land, merits to be bound afterward to the supernal holy land. And he further says on: and not only that, but if he merits it in his lifetime, he merits to have a holy spirit drawn upon him continually; and whoever dwells in another domain has another, foreign spirit drawn upon him - to this point.
